Container.Name: honcho-aio
Container.Description: Honcho — a memory layer for AI agents. Runs PostgreSQL 17+pgvector, Redis, and the Honcho API server (FastAPI) under s6-overlay supervision.
Container.Overview:
Honcho — Persistent Memory for AI Agents

Honcho is an open-source memory engine that gives AI agents structured, persistent memory over multiple sessions. This all-in-one image bundles everything you need:

  • PostgreSQL 17 with the pgvector extension for embedding storage and similarity search.
  • Redis for caching (reduces embedding re-computation).
  • Honcho API server (FastAPI on port 8000) serving the REST and WebSocket endpoints.
  • s6-overlay supervision — Postgres, Redis, and Honcho each run as unprivileged services.

Provider & Model Setup

EMBEDDING_MODEL and CHAT_MODEL use the <provider>/<model> format. The split is on the first /; the model portion may contain nested slashes (e.g. openrouter/openai/gpt-5.4-mini → provider = openrouter, model = openai/gpt-5.4-mini).

Hermes AI Native Integration

Hermes AI can use Honcho as its memory backend natively. After the container is running: 

hermes memory setup

Point Hermes at http://<unraid-lan-ip>:8000. No additional proxy or tunnel required within the LAN.

Important Notes

  • PostgreSQL and Redis are internal only — they listen on 127.0.0.1 inside the container and are not exposed to the host.
  • The chat & deriver model must support tool/function calling. Non-tool-calling completion models will break agent loops.
  • local/ chat uses no cloud fallback — all traffic is routed exclusively to the local endpoint at LOCAL_BASE_URL.
  • At boot, the container probes the embedding model's output dimension. If the dimension does not match EMBEDDING_VECTOR_DIMENSIONS (default 768) the boot fails with a clear error.

Honcho runtime state (config, logs, generated secrets)

Category.Name: Essential Configuration
Category.Description: Required connection secrets and model selection. These fields are always shown.

Config.Name: PostgreSQL Password
Config.Description: Master password for the internal PostgreSQL database. Required — the container will exit with an error on first boot if this is empty. Generate a strong password (e.g. 32 hex chars). Stored as an s6-service secret; never logged or exposed on the process line.

Config.Name: PostgreSQL User
Config.Description: PostgreSQL superuser name. Defaults to "postgres".

Config.Name: PostgreSQL Database
Config.Description: Honcho database name within PostgreSQL. Defaults to "honcho".

Config.Name: Embedding Model
Config.Description: Embedding model in <provider>/<model> format. Example: local/embeddinggemma, openai/text-embedding-3-small, ollama/nomic-embed-text. Supported embedding providers: local, ollama, openai, openrouter, together, gemini.

Config.Name: Chat Model
Config.Description: Chat/completion model in <provider>/<model> format. The model portion retains nested slashes, e.g. openrouter/openai/gpt-5.4-mini (provider=openrouter, model=openai/gpt-5.4-mini). Must support tool/function calling for agent loops. Supported providers: local, ollama, openai, openrouter, together, anthropic, gemini.

Config.Name: Local Provider Base URL
Config.Description: Base URL for the "local/" provider (both embedding and chat). Required when EMBEDDING_MODEL or CHAT_MODEL uses the local provider. Example: http://192.168.1.100:1234/v1 (for LM Studio / LocalAI). When local/ is used for chat there is NO cloud fallback — all traffic is routed exclusively to this endpoint.

Config.Name: Embedding Vector Dimensions
Config.Description: Expected output dimension of the embedding model. At boot the container probes the model's actual dimension; if it does not match this value the boot fails with a clear error. Adjust to match your model (e.g. 1536 for text-embedding-3-small, 1024 for nomic-embed-text-v1.5).

Category.Name: Provider API Keys
Category.Description: API keys for each supported LLM provider. All fields are masked at input. Fill in only the keys for the providers you use (the runtime.env generator reads the relevant key automatically based on your model selection). These are always visible on the main config page for convenience.

Config.Name: OpenAI API Key (also used by OpenRouter & Together)
Config.Description: OpenAI API key. Also used as the credential for OpenRouter and Together (those providers forward the key to their upstream). Required when EMBEDDING_MODEL or CHAT_MODEL uses openai, openrouter, or together.

Config.Name: Anthropic API Key
Config.Description: Anthropic API key for Claude models. Required when CHAT_MODEL uses the anthropic provider. Not used for embeddings (anthropic is chat-only).

Config.Name: Gemini API Key
Config.Description: Google Gemini API key. Required when EMBEDDING_MODEL or CHAT_MODEL uses the gemini provider.

Config.Name: Ollama API Key
Config.Description: Ollama API key. Defaults to "ollama" (what Ollama expects by default). Override if your Ollama instance requires a custom key. Required when EMBEDDING_MODEL or CHAT_MODEL uses the ollama provider.

Config.Name: Local Provider API Key
Config.Description: Optional API key for the "local/" provider. Only needed if your local OpenAI-compatible endpoint (LM Studio, LocalAI, vLLM) requires authentication. Leave blank if the local endpoint is unauthenticated.

Category.Name: Advanced Options
Category.Description: Optional features and tunables: authentication, monitoring, telemetry, Sentry error tracking, webhook secret, deriver concurrency, log verbosity, and namespace isolation. These settings are only shown when toggling the "Advanced View" switch on the template page.

Config.Name: Enable Authentication
Config.Description: Set to "true" to enable JWT-based authentication on the Honcho API. When enabled the container generates a random JWT signing secret on first boot. You may also specify a static secret via AUTH_JWT_SECRET. Defers to AUTH_JWT_SECRET when both are set.

Config.Name: JWT Secret (override)
Config.Description: Static JWT signing secret. When set, the container uses this value instead of auto-generating a random one on first boot. Useful when you need deterministic secrets across restarts or replicas. If left blank the container generates a random 64-byte hex token automatically.

Config.Name: Enable Metrics
Config.Description: Set to "true" to expose Prometheus-compatible metrics at /metrics on the Honcho API port. Useful for scraping into a monitoring stack (Grafana, Prometheus, VictoriaMetrics).

Config.Name: Enable Telemetry
Config.Description: Set to "true" to enable anonymous usage telemetry. Data helps the upstream Honcho team understand deployment patterns and improve the product. No PII is collected.

Config.Name: Enable Sentry
Config.Description: Set to "true" to enable Sentry error tracking. Requires a valid SENTRY_DSN (data source name). Errors are reported to your Sentry project for debugging.

Config.Name: Sentry DSN
Config.Description: Sentry Data Source Name (https://<key>@<org>.ingest.sentry.io/<project>). Required when SENTRY_ENABLED=true. Leave blank if Sentry is disabled.

Config.Name: Webhook Secret
Config.Description: Shared secret for Honcho webhook endpoints. When set, Honcho signs webhook payloads with this secret so receivers can verify authenticity. Generate a random string and share it with your webhook consumer.

Config.Name: Deriver Worker Count
Config.Description: Number of concurrent worker processes for the Honcho deriver (memory derivation and summarization). Increase on multi-core hosts; decrease on constrained hardware. Default: 4.

Config.Name: LLM Log Level
Config.Description: Log verbosity for LLM and embedding calls. One of: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL. DEBUG logs every API round-trip including prompts and responses (noisy but useful for diagnostics). Default: WARNING.

Config.Name: Namespace
Config.Description: Honcho namespace identifier. Each namespace is an isolated data partition — agents in different namespaces cannot see each other's memories. Useful for multi-tenant or multi-agent setups. Default: "default".
